attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is complete only for functional row-value certificates. EF+SAT_U proofs are SAT-semantic over formula labels, so a nonrelativizing extraction theorem or a private-row no-go formalization is still needed.
steps: Assume a row-value certificate A_N(pi,h) is functional and s_N-sound: A_N(pi,h)=1 implies C(h)>s_N for all Boolean h on N-bit rows.
Let R_pi be the set of rows whose h-values can affect acceptance, with |R_pi|=T_N, and suppose A_N(pi,H_N^SAT)=1.
Define h_R to agree with H_N^SAT on R_pi and to be zero outside R_pi. Acceptance is unchanged because A_N only sees rows in R_pi.
Build h_R by OR-ing equality tests for the rows in R_pi and hardwiring the corresponding bits, giving C(h_R)<=O(T_N N).
If T_N=o(s_N/N), then C(h_R)<s_N, contradicting functional soundness. Hence functional certificates proving the source threshold must touch N^{epsilon-o(1)} rows.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation still depends on a concrete DCS-LC syntax audit: accepted certificates must be shown either to provide SAT-semantic labels outside R_N or to fail target preservation. The exact alpha_ad parameters must be computed from the actual opener protocol, not assigned abstractly.
steps: Fix N and a DCS-LC accepted certificate pi_N with adaptive cover parameters tau,a_l,mu_l,omega_l and residual R_N.
Hardwire pi_N and the cover summaries into an unrestricted circuit A_N(x,j) computing the opened label for query (x,j), with size N^{alpha_ad+o(1)} per queried label family.
Use the generator circuit for G_N only as the semantic index ledger; the cover computes labels, and SAT-semantic binding asserts A_N(x,j)=SAT(G_N(x,j)) for x outside R_N.
Build D_N(x)=xor_{j<M_N} A_N(x,j). The fanout over M_N<=N^{q+o(1)} queries gives C(D_N)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ad}+o(1)}.
For each x in R_N, hardwire an equality test on the N input bits and flip D_N(x) when needed. This costs O(|R_N|N)=N^{r+1+o(1)}.
Compare the resulting upper bound with any claimed beta-zero XOR lower bound exponent theta. If theta exceeds max{rho,q+alpha_ad,r+1}, the certificate route contradicts itself.

Validity regime check: the derivation uses the definitions and assumptions listed in the candidate lemmas, preserves the same source object and target object, and is valid only in the stated P vs NP branch model with its declared circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity conditions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves only a conditional route-level falsifier for low-cover certificate carriers. It gives no P != NP lower bound and does not rule out high adaptive-cover, non-natural, advice-free semantic certificates.

assumptions: Model: unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits; hardwiring the accepted certificate, cover summaries, and residual list is allowed for the negative upper-bound contradiction.
Regime: M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, the generator G_N has circuit size N^{rho+o(1)}, and formula lengths L_N=(log N)^d do not add a polynomial-in-N cost.

Uniformity/advice cutoff: advice-free generation is still required for positive extraction to E, but the falsifier direction only needs existence of one fixed low-cover accepted certificate at each N.
Semantic condition: DCS-LC acceptance must certify actual SAT labels outside R_N; ordinary local consistency or cluster soundness alone is not target-preserving.
Residual condition: |R_N|<=N^{r+o(1)} and the exceptional inputs are usable as hardwired equality-test corrections in the nonuniform circuit.
Non-claim boundary: this is a valid route-level obstruction, not a proof of P != NP or of any SAT lower bound.
definitions: source object: DCS-LC_N(pi_N), a fixed accepted DirectClusterSound-style MCSP/MKtP label certificate for the beta-zero XOR SAT-query family, with query count M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, generator overhead N^{rho+o(1)}, and residual set R_N.
target object: H_N^SAT(x)=xor_{j<M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on N-bit inputs, measured by unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuit size C(H_N^SAT).

controlled interface: the certificate opens query labels through an adaptive block cover with exponent alpha_ad=max{tau,max_l(a_l+mu_l),max_l omega_l}, and the opened label for (x,j) is hardwired into a circuit when pi_N is fixed.

target-preserving condition: accepted labels equal SAT(G_N(x,j)) for all x not in R_N and all j, residual corrections are charged on the same N-bit input model, and no change of target language or circuit model is allowed.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If DCS-LC does not bind labels to SAT(G_N(x,j)), the lemma no longer gives an upper bound for H_N^SAT; instead the certificate model is quarantined as not target-preserving.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Finite falsifier theorem for MCSP/MKtP certificate carriers in the beta-zero XOR packet; it upgrades the alpha_ad audit by adding the named SAT-semantic binding and residual ledger.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Low adaptive-cover DCS-LC/MCSP label certificates for the beta-zero XOR family are route-invalid as lower-bound carriers: if the accepted certificate is SAT-semantically bound outside a sparse residual, then it yields C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ad,r+1}+o(1)}. Thus any claimed certificate of C(H_N^SAT)>N^theta with theta above this maximum has a finite falsifier.

assumptions: Model: verifier soundness is syntactic unless it includes a SAT-semantics clause for each generated query.
Same-theory condition: replacing SAT labels by proof labels changes the target object and invalidates transfer to the P vs NP-relevant family.
Cutoff: this is a no-go for the carrier method class, not a lower bound against SAT.
definitions: source object: a DCS-LC or proof-complexity certificate whose verifier checks relations among labels but never enforces label=SAT(G_N(x,j)).
target object: the actual beta-zero XOR language H_N^SAT, not the verifier-induced surrogate XOR of labels.
controlled interface: the observable is the map (x,j)->label_pi(x,j) opened from the certificate.
target-preserving condition: every opened label used in the XOR circuit must be semantically equal to the SAT truth value, except for explicitly charged residual inputs.

equations.latex: D_N(x)=\bigoplus_{j<M_N} label_{\pi_N}(x,j)\ne H_N^{SAT}(x)\text{ on an uncharged set }S_N
equations.valid_when: Valid when the accepted proof labels are locally consistent but not proved SAT-semantic on S_N.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proof of label=SAT(G_N(x,j)) outside R_N repairs the gap; otherwise the route has no valid target-preserving bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantine rule for ordinary soundness-only certificate routes before they enter the theorem packet.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Local proof consistency cannot replace SAT-semantic binding in a beta-zero XOR carrier. A label assignment may satisfy cluster checks while disagreeing with SAT on many generated formulas, so it can certify only an internal proof object, not hardness of H_N^SAT.

assumptions: Nonuniform model: lower-bound refutation may hardwire length-N auxiliary data.
Uniform target model: E extraction cannot use length advice or an unsearchable hard-row selector.

definitions: source object: an advice-selected accepted certificate pi_N or hard row chosen by a nonuniform selector.
target object: either the negative upper bound for H_N^SAT or the positive extraction of an E-uniform hard language.
controlled interface: the selector, certificate, cover summaries, and residual exceptions are either hardwired into nonuniform circuits or generated uniformly for E extraction.
target-preserving condition: positive extraction requires advice-free searchability; negative refutation only requires that the hardwired object computes the same H_N^SAT labels semantically.
